audit.whatIsWrong: The matchup is written as if Swain were melee. content.early opens 'Swain is a melee champion who has to walk into your Flamespitter to trade', and full.phases[0].why / full.breakdown.early both use the template line 'Flamespitter wins every melee level 1 — walk at them.'
audit.why: Swain is a ranged mage. Death's Hand (Q) is 750 range and Nevermove (E) is 850; Rumble's Flamespitter (Q) is a 600-range cone. Swain outranges Rumble's damage ability by 150 units and never has to enter it to farm or poke. The only Rumble tool that matches him at range is Electro-Harpoon (E) at 850. Telling a Rumble player level 1 is free because the enemy is melee will get him poked out of a lane he otherwise wins.
audit.corrected: Level 1 belongs to Swain on range; Rumble's answer is Electro-Harpoon at 850, and he closes to Flamespitter range only from Danger Zone with the harpoon slow already applied.

audit.whatIsWrong: Nevermove is described only as 'his E pull' with advice to 'dodge or outrun' it and 'walk out of its travel path'. The mechanic that actually decides the dodge is never stated.
audit.why: Riot's own text: 'Swain launches a wave of demonic power forward. It then returns to Swain and roots enemies it hits.' The outgoing wave does not root — only the return pass does. That inverts the correct dodge: you step THROUGH the outgoing wave toward Swain rather than running away from it, because running away keeps you inside the return corridor. This is the single highest-value piece of tech in the matchup and it is absent from both layers.
audit.corrected: Nevermove roots on the return pass only — walk through the outgoing wave instead of retreating along its path, then punish the miss with the double harpoon.

audit.whatIsWrong: content.mid says only 'His pull has a meaningful cooldown' — no number anywhere in the matchup. content.whys[3] likewise says 'His pull is on a cooldown'.
audit.why: Nevermove is 12/11.5/11/10.5/10 seconds. At the levels this advice covers (4-5) that is a real, countable 12-to-11 second window, which is long enough to walk him down and crash a wave. Vague cooldown language gives the player nothing to act on.
audit.corrected: State the number: Nevermove is down 12s at rank 1, and that is the window to force the Danger Zone trade.

audit.whatIsWrong: Demonic Ascension is treated as a fixed-duration ultimate to be waited out ('back off and punish the cooldown instead') without explaining why backing off works.
audit.why: Riot's text: 'This form is indefinite as long as Swain drains enemy champions.' The drain radius is 650. Leaving that radius does not merely let you avoid damage — it actively ends his ultimate early, because the form sustains itself only on champion drain. That converts a passive 'back off' into a concrete, aggressive instruction with a number attached.
audit.corrected: Break 650 range and Demonic Ascension expires on its own — walking out ends the ultimate rather than just avoiding it.

audit.whatIsWrong: full.diff is 'EVEN' and full.diffRating is '6/10', but the matchup win rate is 56.45% over 558 games.
audit.why: A 56.45% win rate on a 558-game sample is a clearly favoured lane, not an even one. Every other Rumble entry at this win rate is labelled FAVOURED. I did not propose the edit because 'EVEN' -> 'FAVOURED' cannot survive the ±10% length band, so it needs to be changed by hand or by the applier's enum path.
audit.corrected: diff should read FAVOURED; diffRating closer to 4/10.

audit.why: Grievous Wounds is already core in full.breakdown.late and the itemization report block ('Anti-heal (Oblivion Orb / Executioner's) early — his healing fights your pattern'). This matches the _missing-interactions 'needs-antiheal' entry for Swain, so no edit is needed.

edits.before: Flamespitter wins every melee level 1 — walk at them. Identify how Swain contests the first waves before you commit anything.
edits.after: Swain is ranged — Death's Hand at 750 beats your 600 Flamespitter, so level 1 is his. Farm it and chip with Electro-Harpoon.

edits.before: Flamespitter wins every melee level 1 — walk at them. Respect Swain's Demonic Ascension completely — the first levels are about banking small advantages, not proving a point.
edits.after: Swain is ranged, so there is no free melee level 1 — his Q outranges yours. Respect Nevermove: it roots on the return pass, not the way out, so walk through it.

edits.before: Swain is a melee champion who has to walk into your Flamespitter to trade, which makes Level 1 already yours — just ride 50-100 Heat and walk the Q cone across him every time he steps up to last-hit. At Level 2 you add the Electro-Harpoon slow: if he tries his E pull, pre-cast W for the movement speed burst to walk out of its travel path, then answer with the double-E slow to prevent him escaping your follow-up Q. By Level 3 you have the full pattern — Q through him at Danger Zone, double-E to keep him in the flame, and W to eat any chip he gets back. His E root is the only tool that can flip a trade: if it lands and his W bomb detonates on you while you are silenced from Overheat, he wins the exchange. Never Overheat accidentally in his pull range.
edits.after: Swain is ranged, not melee — Death's Hand at 750 outranges your 600 Flamespitter, so Level 1 is his and you farm it with Electro-Harpoon at 850. At Level 2 the harpoon slow arrives: Nevermove only roots on its RETURN pass, so step through the outgoing wave rather than running down it, then punish the miss with the double-E slow. Whiffs cost him the lane — Death's Hand is 40 mana and Nevermove 50, and a Swain who misses both cannot contest the wave. By Level 3 you have the full pattern — close at Danger Zone, Q through him, double-E to hold him in the flame, W to eat the chip. Nevermove is the one tool that flips a trade: rooted, his W eye lands and Overheat locks your casts out, and he wins. Never Overheat inside 850 of him.

edits.before: Levels 4 and 5 are your best window to punish him for farm. His pull has a meaningful cooldown and if you bait it on your W movement speed burst, the follow-up double-harpoon slow + Danger Zone Flamespitter deals more than he can answer in the window before his next rotation. Freeze the wave on your side of the lane so he must overextend to last-hit, putting him in your range without river-escape access. At Level 6 the dynamic shifts in your favour on the macro axis: Equalizer laid horizontally across the lane or across the brush he needs to walk through makes any all-in by him catastrophically costly. His Demonic Ascension is the danger — if he activates R during a trade at close range, do not fight through it; back off and punish the cooldown instead.
edits.after: Levels 4 and 5 are your best window to punish him for farm. Nevermove is down 12s at rank 1, and if you bait it on your W movement speed burst the follow-up double-harpoon slow plus Danger Zone Flamespitter deals more than he can answer before his next rotation. Freeze the wave on your side so he must overextend to last-hit, putting him in your range without river-escape access. At Level 6 the macro axis shifts to you: Equalizer laid across the brush he needs to walk through makes any all-in by him catastrophically costly. His Demonic Ascension is the danger — if he activates R at close range do not fight through it; step outside 650 and it expires on its own, because the form only sustains while he drains a champion.

edits.before: Swain's Demonic Ascension R gives him a sustained drain that can turn a losing extended fight around — never let him freecast it at close range without your Equalizer as a counter-threat.
edits.after: Demonic Ascension sustains itself only while Swain is draining a champion — step outside its 650 radius and the form ends early, so break range instead of trading through a 120s ultimate.

DATA BUG in champ-data/_kits/rumble.json: Scrap Shield (W) carries flags 'knockup' ("displacement — enables knockup-dependent ults") and 'terrain' ("creates terrain, blocks paths and dashes"). Scrap Shield is a shield plus a movement-speed burst — it displaces nothing and creates no terrain. This bad flag propagates into _missing-interactions.json as 'knockup-enabler' rows for Rumble (visible in the tahmkench, teemo and vayne entries, all claiming 'Both sides carry displacement (Scrap Shield (W) vs ...)'). I ignored every one of those rows. Worth fixing in the kit builder before the flags mislead another pass.

Also ignored: the _missing-interactions 'resistances-invalidated' row for Swain. It is derived from the percentHealth flag on Ravenous Flock, but that flag is there because soul fragments grant permanent max health — Swain is not dealing percent-max-health damage, so 'raw armour or MR is the wrong answer' does not hold. MR is in fact correct against him.
